questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Giza pyramids were built by ancient Egyptians as royal tombs, around 2600–2500 BC.

questions.question: Which empire built the Colosseum in Rome?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum was completed under the Roman Empire in AD 80.

questions.question: Which ancient empire did Cyrus the Great found in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: Cyrus united Medes and Persians.

questions.question: Which Greek city-state is regarded as the birthplace of democracy?
questions.explanation: Athens developed rule by citizens' assembly in the 5th century BC and earlier.

questions.question: In honour of which god were the ancient Olympic Games held?
questions.explanation: The Games honoured Zeus at his sanctuary at Olympia.

questions.question: Which king of Macedon conquered the Persian Empire?
questions.explanation: Alexander overthrew the Persian Empire between 334 and 330 BC.

questions.question: To which goddess was the Parthenon dedicated?
questions.explanation: The Parthenon honoured Athena Parthenos, patron of Athens.

questions.question: Which Spartan king led the famous stand at Thermopylae?
questions.explanation: Leonidas held the pass with about 300 Spartans and allied Greeks.

questions.question: Which two epic poems are attributed to Homer?
questions.explanation: The Iliad tells of the Trojan War; the Odyssey of Odysseus' journey home.

questions.question: Who was Plato's teacher?
questions.explanation: Plato was a student of Socrates and wrote dialogues featuring him.

questions.question: Which period of Greek history followed Alexander the Great's death?
questions.explanation: The Hellenistic period runs from 323 BC to the Roman conquest.

questions.question: Bronze is an alloy of copper and which other metal?
questions.explanation: Bronze is copper alloyed with a small share of tin, which made tools and weapons harder.

questions.question: Which island was the centre of the Minoan civilization?
questions.explanation: The Minoans built palaces and ports on Crete in the Bronze Age.

questions.question: In which modern country was Hattusa, capital of the Hittites?
questions.explanation: Hattusa lies in central Anatolia, in present-day Turkey.

questions.question: In which modern country are the ruins of Troy found?
questions.explanation: The mound of Hisarlik, identified with Troy, lies in north-western Turkey.

questions.question: Which city, with its Lion Gate, was the centre of a Bronze Age Greek civilization?
questions.explanation: Mycenae gave its name to the Mycenaean civilization, which flourished from about 1600 to 1100 BC.

questions.question: In which country is Stonehenge?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge stands on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England.

questions.question: Which Babylonian king is famous for a law code carved on a stone stele?
questions.explanation: Hammurabi's stele lists nearly 300 laws and is now in the Louvre.

questions.question: Whose almost intact tomb did Howard Carter find in the Valley of the Kings?
questions.explanation: Carter found Tutankhamun's tomb with its treasures largely undisturbed.

questions.question: Which English king broke with the Roman Catholic Church and founded the Church of England?
questions.explanation: The break came in the 1530s.

questions.question: Which European country ruled Haiti as the colony of Saint-Domingue?
questions.explanation: Saint-Domingue was France's richest colony.

questions.question: How many prisoners were held in the Bastille when it was stormed on 14 July 1789?
questions.explanation: Only seven prisoners were inside: four forgers, two men judged insane and one nobleman.
questions.misconception: Many people think the Bastille was full of political prisoners when it was stormed.

questions.question: Which two rivers framed Mesopotamia, "the land between the rivers"?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia means "between the rivers": the Tigris and the Euphrates, in what is now mostly Iraq.

questions.question: Whose annual flood made farming possible in ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: The yearly Nile flood left rich black silt, which fed Egyptian agriculture for millennia.

questions.question: What were the Egyptian pyramids mainly built as?
questions.explanation: The pyramids were monumental tombs for pharaohs, meant to secure their afterlife.

questions.question: Which river gave its name to a Bronze Age civilization with cities such as Mohenjo-daro?
questions.explanation: The Indus Valley civilization flourished along the Indus river in present-day Pakistan and India.

questions.question: Which river is often called the cradle of Chinese civilization?
questions.explanation: Early Chinese states grew in the fertile loess plains along the Yellow River.

questions.question: Which Sumerian city, home of the legendary Gilgamesh, is among the world's first cities?
questions.explanation: Uruk, in southern Mesopotamia, grew into one of the first true cities by the fourth millennium BC.

questions.question: What is the picture writing of ancient Egypt called?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphs combined pictures and sound signs and were used for monuments and sacred texts.

questions.question: How many months did the ancient Egyptian civil calendar have?
questions.explanation: The Egyptian civil calendar had 12 months, grouped into three seasons of four months.

questions.question: Which pandemic killed a huge share of Europe's population in the 1340s and 1350s?
questions.explanation: It is estimated to have killed tens of millions across Eurasia.

questions.question: Who was crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day 800?
questions.explanation: The coronation took place in Rome.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: The war in Europe ended in May 1945 and the war in the Pacific in September 1945.

questions.question: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface.

questions.question: Whose assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 set off the First World War?
questions.explanation: The assassination of 28 June 1914 led to Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia.

questions.question: Which leader is best known for non-violent resistance in India's independence movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's methods included boycotts and mass marches.

questions.question: Which system of legal racial segregation did South Africa's National Party formalise from 1948?
questions.explanation: Apartheid classified people by race and separated them by law.

questions.question: How did Napoleon Bonaparte's height compare with that of an average Frenchman of his day?
questions.explanation: He was about 5 pieds 2 pouces in French units, roughly 1.69 m, which was average or slightly above for his time.
questions.misconception: Many people think Napoleon was unusually short.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as president from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: Which West African ruler of the Mali Empire made a famously lavish pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage spread so much gold that it was said to have lowered its value in Cairo.

questions.question: Which Chinese admiral led great treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean in the early 1400s?
questions.explanation: Zheng He commanded seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa in 1532?
questions.explanation: Pizarro seized Atahualpa at Cajamarca.

questions.question: In which city was the House of Wisdom, a great centre of learning under the Abbasid caliphs?
questions.explanation: Baghdad was the Abbasid capital and a hub of translation and science.

questions.question: Which Muslim ruler recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?
questions.explanation: Saladin took Jerusalem in October 1187.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century, high in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.question: Which Germanic people, led by Alaric, sacked Rome in AD 410?
questions.explanation: Alaric's Visigoths entered Rome in 410, the first time in about 800 years that the city fell to a foreign enemy.

questions.question: Which Frankish king is traditionally said to have converted to Catholic Christianity, helping unite the Franks and Gauls?
questions.explanation: Clovis, king of the Franks, was baptised as a Catholic. Many historians place this around 496, though some argue for a later date.

questions.question: Which Frankish leader won the Battle of Tours in 732?
questions.explanation: Charles Martel defeated an army from Umayyad Spain near Tours and Poitiers.

questions.question: In 793 Viking raiders attacked the island monastery of Lindisfarne. Which kingdom was it in?
questions.explanation: Lindisfarne lies off the coast of Northumbria in north-east England.

questions.question: The Danelaw was the part of England under which people's law?
questions.explanation: After the 880s treaty with the Danes, the north-east of England fell under Danish law.

questions.question: Which ship carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620?
questions.explanation: The Mayflower landed at Cape Cod in November 1620, with about 100 passengers.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in 14th-century Italy, notably in Florence.

questions.question: Which French writer wrote the satirical novel Candide?
questions.explanation: Voltaire wrote Candide, which mocks blind optimism and the cruelty of his age.

questions.question: Who co-edited the Encyclopédie with Jean le Rond d'Alembert?
questions.explanation: Diderot edited the Encyclopédie, which aimed to gather and spread all human knowledge.

questions.question: Which work by Rousseau opens with 'Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains'?
questions.explanation: The Social Contract begins with that line and argues that legitimate authority rests on the consent of the governed.

questions.question: Which English philosopher argued that people have natural rights to life, liberty and property?
questions.explanation: Locke held that governments exist to protect these rights and may be replaced if they fail.

questions.question: Which Indian port did Vasco da Gama reach in 1498?
questions.explanation: Gama landed at Calicut on the Malabar coast.

questions.question: Which river did Jacques Cartier explore for France, reaching the sites of Quebec and Montreal?
questions.explanation: He sailed up the St. Lawrence River in the 1530s.

questions.question: The Americas are named after which Italian navigator and mapmaker?
questions.explanation: Martin Waldseemuller used a version of Vespucci's first name on a 1507 map.

questions.question: Which country did John Cabot sail for when he reached North America?
questions.explanation: Cabot, an Italian, sailed under King Henry VII.

questions.question: Which pope called for the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont?
questions.explanation: Urban II made his appeal in November 1095.

questions.question: Which king ordered the Domesday Book survey of England?
questions.explanation: He ordered the survey in 1085, and it was completed in 1086.

questions.question: Otto I, crowned emperor in 962, belonged to which royal dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Ottonians came from Saxony.

questions.question: Notre-Dame de Paris was built in which architectural style?
questions.explanation: Its pointed arches and flying buttresses are typical of Gothic style.

questions.question: Which university in Italy is traditionally regarded as the oldest in the Western world?
questions.explanation: It is usually said to have been founded in 1088.

questions.question: Which city did the Fourth Crusade sack in 1204?
questions.explanation: The crusaders attacked the Christian city of Constantinople rather than reaching the Holy Land.

questions.question: Which Scottish king won the Battle of Bannockburn?
questions.explanation: Robert the Bruce defeated Edward II's army in 1314.

questions.question: Which event of October 1929 opened the Great Depression?
questions.explanation: Stock prices collapsed in New York, and the crisis spread worldwide.

questions.question: In which year did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany?
questions.explanation: President Hindenburg appointed him on 30 January 1933.

questions.question: Which British prime minister signed the Munich Agreement in 1938?
questions.explanation: Chamberlain returned promising 'peace for our time'.

questions.question: Which country did Germany annex in March 1938 in the Anschluss?
questions.explanation: German troops entered Austria and it was merged into the Reich.

questions.question: Which city was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate?
questions.explanation: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus from 661 to 750.

questions.question: Which caliph had the Dome of the Rock built in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The shrine was built under the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik.

questions.question: Which city was the capital of the Caliphate of Cordoba in al-Andalus?
questions.explanation: Cordoba became one of the largest cities in Europe under its caliphs.

questions.question: At the Battle of Talas, the Abbasid Caliphate fought which Chinese dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Abbasids defeated the Tang army by the Talas River in Central Asia.

questions.question: Ibn Sina, known in Latin as Avicenna, wrote the Canon of what?
questions.explanation: The Canon of Medicine was used as a textbook for centuries in Europe and the Islamic world.

questions.question: In which country was the traveller Ibn Battuta born?
questions.explanation: He was born in Tangier in 1304.

questions.question: Which people besieged and sacked Baghdad in 1258?
questions.explanation: A Mongol army ended the Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad.

questions.question: Which North African city did the Vandals capture in AD 439?
questions.explanation: Gaiseric took Carthage in 439.

questions.question: Which church did Justinian rebuild in Constantinople?
questions.explanation: Hagia Sophia was rebuilt after fire in the Nika riots.

questions.question: Which emperor gave his name to the plague that began in 541?
questions.explanation: The Plague of Justinian began in 541.

questions.question: Which Frankish king converted to Catholic Christianity around 500?
questions.explanation: Clovis was baptised.

questions.question: Who founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.explanation: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206 after uniting the Mongol tribes.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
questions.explanation: William of Normandy defeated King Harold at Hastings in 1066.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The wall was opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.

questions.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The Revolution began in 1789, famously with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July.

questions.question: The Treaty of Versailles formally ended which war?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919 and formally ended World War I with Germany.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: It began in Britain in the 18th century, driven by textiles, coal and steam power.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The Titanic struck an iceberg and sank on 15 April 1912.

questions.question: Who became the first person in space in 1961?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.question: The Meiji Restoration ended the rule of shoguns from which family?
questions.explanation: The Tokugawa shogunate had ruled since 1603.

questions.question: In which city did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
questions.explanation: Petrograd was the name of Saint Petersburg at the time.

questions.question: On which island was Napoleon Bonaparte born?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio, on an island that France had just acquired from Genoa.

questions.question: Which law code of 1804 gave France a single civil law and became a model for many other countries?
questions.explanation: The Civil Code of 1804 declared citizens equal before the law and protected property.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics and later won a second in Chemistry in 1911.

questions.question: Who was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for most of World War II?
questions.explanation: Churchill led the wartime government from May 1940 to July 1945.

questions.question: At which assembly in 1521 was Martin Luther ordered to recant his writings?
questions.explanation: Luther refused to retract, saying his conscience was bound.

questions.question: Luther translated the New Testament into which language?
questions.explanation: His translation helped shape modern German.

questions.question: In which city did John Calvin lead the Reformation?
questions.explanation: Calvin settled in Geneva in 1536 and again in 1541.

questions.question: The St. Bartholomew's Day massacre of 1572 took place first in which city?
questions.explanation: Violence began in Paris and spread across France.

questions.question: Who founded the Society of Jesus, the Jesuits?
questions.explanation: Ignatius, a Basque from Spain, founded the order with companions.

questions.question: Which banking family dominated Florence for much of the 15th century and funded Renaissance artists?
questions.explanation: The Medici bank made the family rich, and they sponsored artists such as Botticelli and Michelangelo.

questions.question: Which pope commissioned Michelangelo to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.explanation: Pope Julius II ordered the work, which Michelangelo painted from 1508.

questions.question: Which Florentine wrote The Prince, a book on gaining and keeping political power?
questions.explanation: Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513, and it was published in 1532.

questions.question: In which English town was William Shakespeare born?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.

questions.question: Which English humanist wrote Utopia, describing an imaginary island society?
questions.explanation: Thomas More published Utopia in 1516.

questions.question: Who painted The School of Athens, a fresco in the Vatican?
questions.explanation: Raphael painted it between about 1509 and 1511.

questions.question: In which year did the Boston Tea Party take place?
questions.explanation: On 16 December 1773 colonists threw tea of the British East India Company into Boston Harbor.

questions.question: In which year did the Great Fire of Rome break out?
questions.explanation: The Great Fire began in July AD 64.

questions.question: The Edict of Milan, protecting Christians, was issued in
questions.explanation: Constantine and Licinius issued the Edict in 313.

questions.question: Who began the Appian Way in 312 BC?
questions.explanation: The censor Appius Claudius Caecus started it.

questions.question: According to tradition, in which year was Rome founded?
questions.explanation: Roman tradition, fixed by Varro, dates the founding of Rome to 753 BC.

questions.question: According to tradition, in which year did Rome become a republic?
questions.explanation: The last king was traditionally expelled in 509 BC and the Republic founded.

questions.question: In which year did the First Punic War begin?
questions.explanation: Rome and Carthage went to war over Sicily in 264 BC.

questions.question: Which Roman general defeated Hannibal at Zama?
questions.explanation: Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal at Zama in North Africa.

questions.question: About how long did Caesar's conquest of Gaul last?
questions.explanation: Caesar fought in Gaul from 58 to 50 BC.

questions.question: Who formed the First Triumvirate with Caesar and Pompey?
questions.explanation: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus made a private political alliance.

questions.question: How long did a regular Roman consul's term last?
questions.explanation: Consuls were elected annually.

questions.question: The name 'Zimbabwe' is generally traced to a Shona phrase meaning roughly what?
questions.explanation: It comes from dzimba dza mabwe, 'houses of stone'.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador led the conquest of the Aztec Empire?
questions.explanation: Cortés landed in 1519 and allied with peoples hostile to the Aztecs.

questions.question: Which two powers formed the core of the Central Powers in the First World War?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria later joined Germany and Austria-Hungary.

questions.question: In which month of 1914 was Archduke Franz Ferdinand assassinated?
questions.explanation: He was shot on 28 June 1914, and the July crisis followed.

questions.question: What was the name for the ground between opposing trenches on the Western Front?
questions.explanation: No man's land was exposed to machine guns and shellfire.

questions.question: Which treaty took Russia out of the First World War in March 1918?
questions.explanation: The Bolsheviks signed it with the Central Powers, giving up large territories.

questions.question: In which year did the United States enter the First World War?
questions.explanation: The US declared war on Germany in April 1917.

questions.question: Which country did Germany invade on 1 September 1939, starting the Second World War in Europe?
questions.explanation: Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later.

questions.question: Which Japanese city was hit by the first atomic bomb in August 1945?
questions.explanation: Hiroshima was bombed on 6 August 1945 and Nagasaki three days later.

questions.question: In which year did Japan attack Pearl Harbor?
questions.explanation: The attack came on 7 December 1941 and brought the US into the war.

questions.question: About how many African countries became independent in 1960, often called the Year of Africa?
questions.explanation: Around seventeen African countries gained independence in 1960.

questions.question: For about how long did the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda last?
questions.explanation: The killings ran for roughly 100 days, from April to July 1994.

questions.question: In which year did Britain's Parliament abolish the slave trade throughout its empire?
questions.explanation: The Slave Trade Act of 1807 ended the trade, but not slavery itself.

questions.question: For about how many years was Ethiopia occupied by Fascist Italy, from 1936?
questions.explanation: Italy occupied Ethiopia from 1936 until British and Ethiopian forces freed it in 1941.

questions.question: In which year did the Suez Crisis occur, after Egypt nationalised the canal?
questions.explanation: Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal Company in July 1956.

questions.question: In which year did the Second Boer War end?
questions.explanation: The war ended with the Peace of Vereeniging in 1902.

questions.question: In which year did the United States buy the Louisiana Territory from France?
questions.explanation: The Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States in 1803.

questions.question: How many years did the American Civil War last, from 1861 to 1865?
questions.explanation: The war lasted from 1861 to 1865.

questions.question: In which year did Brazil declare independence from Portugal?
questions.explanation: Brazil declared independence on 7 September 1822.

questions.question: In which year did the Panama Canal open to ships?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal opened in August 1914.

questions.question: In which year did the Mexican Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The revolution began in November 1910.

questions.question: In which year did Fidel Castro's revolution take power in Cuba?
questions.explanation: Castro's forces entered Havana in January 1959.

questions.question: In which year did the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo end the Mexican-American War?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed in February 1848.

questions.question: In which year did Canadian Confederation create the Dominion of Canada?
questions.explanation: Canada was formed on 1 July 1867.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China, founding the Qin dynasty?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BC and took the title of first emperor.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome?
questions.explanation: Hannibal made the crossing in 218 BC during the Second Punic War.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which writing system?
questions.explanation: Its text appears in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek, which let Champollion crack hieroglyphs in the 1820s.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor ordered the construction of a wall across northern Britain in AD 122?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall marked the northern frontier of Roman Britain.

questions.question: Which war, fought from 431 to 404 BC, pitted Athens against Sparta and their allies?
questions.explanation: Sparta won, ending Athenian dominance.

questions.question: Which of these gaps in time is the LONGEST?
choices: From Cleopatra VII to the fall of Constantinople in 1453
From the fall of Constantinople to the Moon landing
From Cleopatra VII to the Moon landing
From the Great Pyramid of Giza to Cleopatra VII
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid (about 2560 BC) is about 2,500 years before Cleopatra; the other gaps are about 2,000, 1,480 and 520 years.
questions.misconception: Many people think Cleopatra lived about when the Great Pyramid was built.

questions.question: Which people founded the Qing dynasty, China's last imperial dynasty?
questions.explanation: Manchu leaders from the north-east took Beijing in 1644.

questions.question: Which Ottoman reform era, starting in 1839, aimed to modernise the state?
questions.explanation: The Tanzimat reorganised law, taxes and the army along European lines.

questions.question: Which dynasty made Shia Islam the state religion of Persia from 1501?
questions.explanation: Shah Ismail I founded the Safavid state and imposed Twelver Shia Islam.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan ordered it after she died in 1631.

questions.question: Which Russian tsar sold Alaska to the United States in 1867?
questions.explanation: Russia sold the remote territory because it was costly to defend and hard to reach.

questions.question: In which year did the Russo-Japanese War end?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Portsmouth, signed in 1905 with US mediation, ended the war.

questions.question: Which treaty ended the First Opium War in 1842 and ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Nanking opened Chinese ports and ceded Hong Kong Island.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Rebellion against the East India Company break out?
questions.explanation: The rebellion of 1857 began with a mutiny of Indian soldiers.

questions.question: About how long did the Tokugawa shogunate rule Japan, from 1603 to 1868?
questions.explanation: 1868 minus 1603 gives about 265 years of Tokugawa rule.

questions.question: On which date in August 1945 was the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima?
questions.explanation: Hiroshima was bombed on 6 August 1945.

questions.question: In which year did Kublai Khan proclaim the Yuan dynasty in China?
questions.explanation: Kublai Khan declared the Yuan dynasty in 1271.

questions.question: In which year did Saigon fall, ending the Vietnam War?
questions.explanation: Saigon fell on 30 April 1975.

questions.question: In which year did the armistice halt the fighting in the Korean War?
questions.explanation: The armistice was signed on 27 July 1953.

questions.question: How many years separate the fall of Constantinople (1453) from Columbus's first voyage (1492)?
How many years separate the French Revolution (1789) from the fall of the Berlin Wall (1989)?
questions.explanation: 1989 minus 1789 is exactly 200.

questions.question: How many years separate the traditional fall of Western Rome (476) from Charlemagne's coronation (800)?
questions.explanation: 800 minus 476 is 324.

questions.question: About how many years passed between the end of World War I (1918) and the start of World War II (1939)?
questions.explanation: Roughly 21 years separated the two wars.

questions.question: How many years separate Gagarin's flight (1961) from the Apollo 11 landing (1969)?
questions.explanation: 1969 minus 1961 is 8.

questions.question: How many years separate the end of World War II (1945) from the dissolution of the Soviet Union (1991)?
Traditionally, how many years separate the first Olympic Games (776 BC) from the founding of Rome (753 BC)?
questions.explanation: 776 minus 753 is 23.

questions.question: How many years separate the Titanic's sinking (1912) from the Moon landing (1969)?
On which date did construction of the Berlin Wall begin?
questions.explanation: Barbed wire went up overnight, and a concrete wall followed.

questions.question: About how many days did the Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 last?
questions.explanation: It ran from 16 to 28 October 1962.

questions.question: In which year did Saigon fall to North Vietnamese forces?
questions.explanation: Saigon fell on 30 April 1975 and was later renamed Ho Chi Minh City.

questions.question: Who was the first American to orbit the Earth, in 1962?
questions.explanation: Glenn orbited three times in February 1962, after Shepard's short 1961 flight.

questions.question: In which year were the Helsinki Accords signed?
questions.explanation: They were signed in August 1975 by 35 states.

questions.question: How many union republics did the Soviet Union have when it dissolved?
questions.explanation: Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and twelve others became independent states.

questions.question: Which conference of July and August 1945, held near Berlin, followed Yalta?
questions.explanation: Truman, Stalin and Churchill, later Attlee, met at Potsdam.

questions.question: Who warned in a 1946 speech at Fulton, Missouri, that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe?
questions.explanation: Churchill spoke of a curtain from the Baltic to the Adriatic.

questions.question: About how much aid did the Marshall Plan give to Europe between 1948 and 1951?
questions.explanation: The US sent roughly 13 billion dollars to rebuild western Europe.

questions.question: About how long did the Soviet blockade of West Berlin last in 1948 and 1949?
questions.explanation: It began in June 1948 and ended in May 1949.

questions.question: How many countries were founding members of NATO in 1949?
questions.explanation: The founders included the US, Canada, Britain, France and eight other countries.

questions.question: In which year was the armistice that ended the fighting in Korea signed?
questions.explanation: The armistice was signed in July 1953, but no peace treaty followed.

questions.question: In which year did the Soviet Union test its first atomic bomb?
questions.explanation: The Soviet test in August 1949 ended the US nuclear monopoly.

questions.question: In which year did Mao Zedong proclaim the People's Republic of China?
questions.explanation: Mao proclaimed it in Beijing on 1 October 1949.

questions.question: By 1914, about what share of Africa was under European control?
questions.explanation: Only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent states in 1914.

questions.question: In which year did Britain pass the Act banning the slave trade across its empire?
questions.explanation: The Slave Trade Act of 1807 made the trade illegal, while slavery itself ended later.

questions.question: Which 1842 treaty ended the First Opium War and ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain?
questions.explanation: China also opened five ports to British trade under the treaty.

questions.question: In which year did the British Crown take over direct rule of India from the East India Company?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act of 1858 followed the great uprising of 1857.

questions.question: In which year did the First Fleet arrive in Australia to found a British colony?
questions.explanation: The First Fleet reached Botany Bay in January 1788 and founded the colony of New South Wales.

questions.question: Which three present-day countries made up French Indochina?
questions.explanation: France built this union in the late 1800s and left it in 1954.

questions.question: Which company founded in 1602, one of the first to sell shares to the public, ran much of the Dutch empire in Asia?
questions.explanation: The VOC was founded two years after its English rival.

questions.question: In which year did Algeria gain independence from France?
questions.explanation: Independence was proclaimed on 5 July 1962, after the Evian Accords.

questions.question: On which date did India become independent from Britain?
questions.explanation: Pakistan became independent a day earlier, on 14 August 1947.

questions.question: In which year did the Netherlands formally recognise Indonesian sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Independence was proclaimed in 1945, but recognition came after a war in 1949.

questions.question: In which year did the Algerian War of Independence begin?
questions.explanation: The FLN launched its uprising on 1 November 1954.

questions.question: In which year did Ghana gain independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: Ghana became independent on 6 March 1957.

questions.question: In which year did Nasser nationalise the Suez Canal?
questions.explanation: Nasser seized the canal company in July 1956.

questions.question: In which year did France lose the Battle of Dien Bien Phu?
questions.explanation: The defeat in May 1954 ended French rule in Indochina.

questions.question: For about how many years was Nelson Mandela imprisoned?
questions.explanation: He was jailed in 1962 and freed in 1990.

questions.question: In which year was Hagia Sophia in Constantinople completed under Emperor Justinian?
questions.explanation: Built in under six years, Hagia Sophia was dedicated on 27 December 537.

questions.question: In which year did the Treaty of Verdun divide the Carolingian Empire among Charlemagne's grandsons?
questions.explanation: The 843 treaty split the empire into West, Middle and East Francia.

questions.question: Which monk of Jarrow wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, completed around 731?
questions.explanation: Bede is often called the father of English history.

questions.question: Whose expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the globe between 1519 and 1522?
questions.explanation: Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano led the surviving ship home.

questions.question: Which empire was ruled by Suleiman the Magnificent?
questions.explanation: Suleiman ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1520 to 1566, at its height of power.

questions.question: In which German city did Gutenberg set up his printing workshop?
questions.explanation: Mainz on the Rhine was his home town and workplace.

questions.question: Which thinker's 1748 book The Spirit of the Laws argued for separating legislative, executive and judicial power?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu argued that dividing power prevents any one person or group from becoming a tyrant.

questions.question: In which year did Adam Smith publish The Wealth of Nations?
questions.explanation: The Wealth of Nations appeared in 1776 and became a founding text of modern economics.

questions.question: Which Prussian king, reigning from 1740 to 1786, corresponded with Voltaire and was called an enlightened despot?
questions.explanation: Frederick the Great reformed laws and tolerated faiths, yet ruled as an absolute monarch.

questions.question: Which German philosopher answered 'What is Enlightenment?' in 1784 with the motto 'Dare to know'?
questions.explanation: Kant defined enlightenment as leaving behind self-imposed immaturity by thinking for yourself.

questions.question: In which year did Bartolomeu Dias round the southern tip of Africa?
questions.explanation: Dias reached the Cape of Good Hope area in 1488, ten years before Vasco da Gama reached India.

questions.question: Which sequence of voyages is in the correct order?
choices: Dias round Africa, Columbus to the Americas, Gama to India, Cabral to Brazil
Gama to India, Dias round Africa, Columbus to the Americas, Cabral to Brazil
Columbus to the Americas, Dias round Africa, Gama to India, Cabral to Brazil
Dias round Africa, Gama to India, Columbus to the Americas, Cabral to Brazil
questions.explanation: The dates are 1488 (Dias), 1492 (Columbus), 1498 (Gama) and 1500 (Cabral).

questions.question: In 1077 King Henry IV of Germany did penance at Canossa before which pope?
questions.explanation: The Investiture Controversy was a dispute over who could appoint bishops.

questions.question: Which invention by James Hargreaves let one worker spin several threads at once?
questions.explanation: The spinning jenny, invented in the 1760s, multiplied what one spinner could produce.

questions.question: Which railway, opened in 1825, is regarded as the first public line to use steam locomotives?
questions.explanation: George Stephenson's Locomotion No. 1 hauled the first train on the Stockton and Darlington Railway.

questions.question: The British Factory Act of 1833 banned children below which age from working in textile mills?
questions.explanation: Children aged nine to thirteen were limited to nine hours a day, and inspectors were appointed to enforce the law.

questions.question: In which London building was the Great Exhibition of 1851 held?
questions.explanation: Joseph Paxton designed the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park to show off the world's industry.

questions.question: What did Henry Bessemer's process of 1856 make cheap and plentiful?
questions.explanation: Blowing air through molten iron burned off impurities, making steel affordable for rails, ships and bridges.

questions.question: Which British city was nicknamed 'Cottonopolis' for its mills?
questions.explanation: Manchester became the centre of cotton spinning and weaving in the 1800s.

questions.question: In which year did German hyperinflation reach its peak?
questions.explanation: In 1923 prices rose so fast that banknotes were worth almost nothing.

questions.question: In which year did Mussolini come to power after the March on Rome?
questions.explanation: The king asked him to form a government in October 1922.

questions.question: In which years was the Spanish Civil War fought?
questions.explanation: The war began in July 1936 and ended with a Nationalist victory in 1939.

questions.question: In which year did Tariq ibn Ziyad cross into Iberia and begin the Muslim conquest of Visigothic Spain?
questions.explanation: In 711 Tariq's army crossed from North Africa and defeated the Visigothic king Roderic.

questions.question: In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
questions.explanation: East Germany began building the Wall in August 1961.

questions.question: In which year did the Chernobyl nuclear disaster occur?
questions.explanation: Reactor 4 exploded on 26 April 1986.

questions.question: In which year did the Soviet Union invade Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Soviet troops entered Afghanistan in December 1979.

questions.question: In which year did the Iranian Revolution overthrow the Shah?
questions.explanation: The Shah left Iran in January 1979.

questions.question: In which year did the Tiananmen Square protests take place?
questions.explanation: The protests and their suppression took place in the spring of 1989.

questions.question: In which year was the Falklands War fought?
questions.explanation: Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands in April 1982.

questions.question: On which date in 1990 was Germany formally reunified?
questions.explanation: Germany celebrates reunification on 3 October.

questions.question: Who was the last Western Roman emperor, deposed in 476?
questions.explanation: Odoacer deposed the boy emperor.

questions.question: The Goths defeated Emperor Valens at Adrianople in
questions.explanation: Adrianople was fought in 378.

questions.question: The final Byzantine-Sasanian war ended in
questions.explanation: It ended in 628.

questions.question: In which year was Magna Carta sealed by King John of England?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede in 1215, limiting the king's powers.

questions.question: The Hundred Years' War was fought mainly between which two kingdoms?
questions.explanation: It lasted from 1337 to 1453, with periods of truce, between England and France.

questions.question: Only one reasonably complete Viking-age helmet has been found in Scandinavia. Which find is it?
questions.explanation: The Gjermundbu helmet (10th century) is a rounded cap with a face guard and has no horns. Sutton Hoo is Anglo-Saxon.
questions.misconception: Many people think Viking warriors wore horned helmets in battle.

questions.question: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explanation: The crisis lasted thirteen days in October 1962 and brought the US and USSR close to nuclear war.

questions.question: Which Belgian king held the Congo Free State as a personal possession?
questions.explanation: The Congo Free State was Leopold's private colony until 1908.

questions.question: In which year did Napoleon seize power in the coup of 18 Brumaire?
questions.explanation: The coup of 18 Brumaire, on 9 November 1799, overthrew the Directory.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Trafalgar fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Trafalgar was fought on 21 October 1805 off the Spanish coast.

questions.question: Which battle of December 1805, often called Napoleon's masterpiece, defeated Russia and Austria?
questions.explanation: Austerlitz is also known as the Battle of the Three Emperors.

questions.question: What was the aim of Napoleon's Continental System, launched in 1806?
choices: To cut off Britain's trade with Europe
questions.explanation: It tried to ruin British commerce by closing the ports of the continent to British goods.

questions.question: Napoleon's army that invaded Russia in 1812 numbered roughly how many men?
questions.explanation: The Grande Armée crossed the Niemen in June 1812. Estimates run from about 450,000 to over 600,000 men.

questions.question: In which year did Napoleon die?
questions.explanation: Napoleon died on 5 May 1821, in exile.

questions.question: In which year was The Communist Manifesto published?
questions.explanation: Marx and Engels published it in 1848.

questions.question: Which century is usually called the Age of Enlightenment?
questions.explanation: The Enlightenment flourished in the 1700s.

questions.question: In which year did Louis Pasteur first test his rabies vaccine on a person?
questions.explanation: Pasteur treated a boy, Joseph Meister, in 1885.

questions.question: In which year did New Zealand give women the vote in national elections, a world first for a self-governing country?
questions.explanation: New Zealand's women won the vote in 1893.

questions.question: In which year did Thomas Edison demonstrate a practical incandescent light bulb?
questions.explanation: Edison's lamp worked in late 1879.

questions.question: In which year was the Gregorian calendar introduced by Pope Gregory XIII?
questions.explanation: The new calendar began in October 1582.

questions.question: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
questions.explanation: The first prizes were awarded in 1901, five years after Nobel's death.

questions.question: In which year was the Peace of Augsburg agreed?
questions.explanation: The 1555 peace allowed Lutheran and Catholic rulers in the Holy Roman Empire to choose their state's religion.

questions.question: In which year did Henry IV of France issue the Edict of Nantes?
questions.explanation: The edict granted Huguenots limited rights of worship.

questions.question: In which year did the Council of Trent end?
questions.explanation: The council ran in three phases from 1545 to 1563.

questions.question: In which year was the dome of Florence Cathedral completed by Filippo Brunelleschi?
questions.explanation: The dome was finished in 1436 and the cathedral was consecrated that year.

questions.question: In which year did the Treaty of Paris recognise American independence?
questions.explanation: Britain signed the Treaty of Paris on 3 September 1783, ending the American Revolutionary War.

questions.question: In which month of 1789 was the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen adopted?
questions.explanation: The National Assembly adopted it on 26 August 1789.

questions.question: Which Jacobin leader of the Committee of Public Safety was guillotined on 28 July 1794?
questions.explanation: Robespierre fell in the coup of 9 Thermidor and went to the guillotine the next day.

questions.question: Which Venezuelan-born leader helped liberate Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia from Spanish rule?
questions.explanation: Bolívar led armies across the Andes in campaigns from the 1810s to the 1820s.

questions.question: Which French king abdicated in the February Revolution of 1848?
questions.explanation: Louis-Philippe gave up the throne on 24 February 1848 and fled to England.

questions.question: Which Dutch prince landed in England in 1688 and then reigned jointly with his wife Mary?
questions.explanation: William III and Mary II became joint monarchs after James II fled.

questions.question: In which year did the Paris Commune rule the capital?
questions.explanation: The Paris Commune governed the city from March to May 1871.

questions.question: The battle of Actium was fought in
questions.explanation: Octavian beat Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BC.

questions.question: About how long did the Pax Romana last?
questions.explanation: It is dated from 27 BC to AD 180.

questions.question: Who was the first of the Five Good Emperors, ruling AD 96 to 98?
questions.explanation: Nerva began the sequence.

questions.question: Rome reached its greatest territorial extent under Trajan in AD
questions.explanation: Trajan died in AD 117 with the empire at its largest.

questions.question: In which century BC did Ashoka's reign begin?
questions.explanation: He ruled from about 268 BC.

questions.question: Where was the Olmec heartland?
choices: The Gulf Coast lowlands of Mexico
questions.explanation: It lay in the present-day Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco.

questions.question: The Schlieffen Plan aimed to defeat which country first?
questions.explanation: Germany planned to knock out France quickly, then turn on Russia.

questions.question: About how long did the Battle of Verdun last?
questions.explanation: It lasted from February to December 1916.

questions.question: About how many British casualties were there on the first day of the Somme, 1 July 1916?
questions.explanation: Roughly 57,000 casualties, about 19,000 of them killed, made it the bloodiest day in British army history.

questions.question: In which month of 1940 did Germany launch its attack on France and the Low Countries?
questions.explanation: The offensive began on 10 May 1940 and France fell within weeks.

questions.question: In which month did Germany launch Operation Barbarossa?
questions.explanation: The invasion of the Soviet Union began on 22 June 1941.

questions.question: The 1943 Battle of Kursk is often described as the largest what in history?
questions.explanation: Thousands of tanks clashed in the summer of 1943.

questions.question: On which date did the D-Day landings in Normandy take place?
questions.explanation: Allied troops landed on 6 June 1944.

questions.question: Roughly how many Jewish people were murdered in the Holocaust?
questions.explanation: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murdered about six million Jews.

questions.question: In which year is the fall of the Western Roman Empire traditionally dated?
questions.explanation: In 476 the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed by Odoacer.

questions.question: At least how many people are estimated to have died in the Taiping Rebellion of 1850 to 1864?
questions.explanation: Estimates run from about 20 to 30 million deaths, making it one of the deadliest wars in history.

questions.question: How much did the United States pay Spain for the Philippines under the 1898 Treaty of Paris?
questions.explanation: The United States paid $20 million as part of the treaty.

questions.question: Who was the Czechoslovak Communist leader behind the Prague Spring reforms?
questions.explanation: Dubček promised 'socialism with a human face'.

questions.question: About how many African countries gained independence in 1960?
questions.explanation: The year became known as the Year of Africa.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor, ruling from 1556 to 1605, is known for his policy of religious tolerance?
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished the tax on non-Muslims and welcomed scholars of many faiths.

questions.question: In which year did Spain and Portugal sign the Treaty of Tordesillas?
questions.explanation: The treaty divided newly found lands outside Europe between the two crowns along a line west of the Cape Verde islands.

questions.question: In which year did Vasco Nunez de Balboa sight the Pacific Ocean from the Americas?
questions.explanation: Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama and saw the Pacific in September 1513.

questions.question: In which year was the first lasting transatlantic telegraph cable completed?
questions.explanation: A cable of 1858 failed within weeks, but the one laid by the Great Eastern in 1866 lasted.

questions.question: Which German engineer received a patent in 1886 for the Motorwagen, regarded as the first practical car?
questions.explanation: Benz's three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen was powered by a small petrol engine.

questions.question: In which year did Attila the Hun die?
questions.explanation: Attila died in 453.

questions.question: The Roman Empire was permanently divided East and West in
questions.explanation: Theodosius I died in 395.

questions.question: The Third Servile War led by Spartacus began in
questions.explanation: Spartacus escaped from a gladiator school in 73 BC.

questions.question: Which German geographer coined the term 'Silk Road' in 1877?
questions.explanation: The name is modern: Richthofen used Seidenstrasse for these trade routes.
